passage:
Carrie helped her parents at their night market stand. They sold fried noodles. Her job was to take orders and give change.
At first, she moved slowly. She mixed up two orders and gave one customer the wrong coins. Her father corrected her quietly.
After a few nights, Carrie became faster. She learned to listen carefully even when the market was noisy. She also learned to smile when customers were impatient.
One evening, a classmate saw her working and said, "You look so serious."
Carrie laughed. School homework was hard, but night market work was hard in another way. It taught her math, manners, memory, and patience all at once.
